    Finding the Gantt's density

    2026-10-27 · Fisheries Evaluation Studies, 23 rows · 1440×900 viewport, head card scrolled away

    Three things set how much plan you can read at once: row height, the outline column's width, and whether About is open. Each variant below is the running chart with only those changed. The numbers are measured, not estimated.

    Row height decides rows in view: tactile shows 13 of 23 rows, compact 20. But the bigger loss was never row height. At 1440 wide, the 420px outline is wider than the timeline whenever About is open. Dropping the per-row level word (see Levels) lets the outline shrink to 280px, which gives the timeline 36% more width with About open.

    Row height

    The About pane

    Levels

    Program, Study, Sub-study, Task and Milestone are drawn alike today: every row carries its level word, and every name sits at one size. They aren't alike. Parents summarize; Tasks and Milestones are what you plan and move.

    The rules

    1. Only Tasks and Milestones are things you move. They get the full bar, its depth and its grips. Parents are summaries of their children: thin brackets, no depth, never grabbable-looking.
    2. Hierarchy by weight and indent, not words. The column header names the levels once; no row repeats its level.
    3. Weight steps down the tree. Program 650, Study 600, Sub-study 550 in secondary, Task 450 in primary. Tasks are the content and read clearly; parents are structure.
    4. A Milestone is a moment at a Task's level. A diamond at the Task indent, no bar, named like a task.
    5. Programs are sections once a plan has more than one: the Program row becomes a band and the rows beneath it start fresh.
    6. One row height for every level. The difference is weight and mark, not height. Mixed heights break the timeline's rhythm and the drag arithmetic.
    7. Budget on Tasks; parents show the rolled-up total in secondary.

    Scheduled dates

    Scheduled dates are fixed from outside the plan: here the winter-freshet tagging season and the encroachment permits. They hold when a cascade comes through, which is why a drag can stop short. Today the only sign is a square corner.

    Seeing a cascade before it happens

    Hover or press a bar and the chart shows what a drag will move with it: every successor, then theirs, stopping at a Scheduled row because it holds. The readout adds a "Moves with it" line with the count. Shown on Regional receiver network build-out.

    Recommendation

    • Medium rows (34px rows, 20px bars) with the tactile look.
    • Ladder levels and the rules above, which free the outline to 280px.
    • About folded by default below 1600px wide; it opens from its rail.
    • Scheduled as a pin.
    • Spotlight for the cascade preview, on hover and while pressed.

    Together: 17 of 23 rows and 528px of timeline with About open, or 756px with it folded, against 13 rows and 388px today.
